react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome is anchored by a coordinated shift in androgen and estrogen steroid hormone metabolism. Across three complementary paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA, and mummichog m/z-network activity — the top pathway is steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism (KEGG:hsa00140 / KEGG:map00150 in ORA; MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism in mummichog), with FDR as low as 1.34e-13 (RaMP) and p=8.39e-06 (MetaboAnalystR). Five of the eight input metabolites — dehydroepiandrosterone (C01227), testosterone (C00535), estrone (C00468), 17β-estradiol (C00951), and 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one / dihydrotestosterone (C03917) — map as driver compounds within this pathway cluster, each confirmed via their InChIKey first-block uniqueness (8 distinct block-14s, zero structural conflicts). Mummichog reports a 13/13 input-to-pathway overlap for the androgen/estrogen network and a 12/12 overlap for the C21-steroid sub-pathway, indicating near-complete representation of the relevant steroid nodes. Three remaining inputs — 5,6,7,8-tetrahydrobiopterin (C00272), spermidine (C00315), and S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (C00021) — appear as secondary hits in tyrosine/biopterin metabolism (MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism rank 3, p=0.028) and the urea-cycle/amino-group module (rank 2, p=0.028), consistent with their biological roles as cofactors for aromatic amino-acid hydroxylases and as methyl-group donors in polyamine biosynthesis, respectively. The cross-paradigm consensus is unambiguous: the dominant biological signal is a global perturbation of the C21 steroid hormone biosynthesis and interconversion network, with five driver metabolites driving the effect. Secondary cofactor/polyamine changes are present but rank far below the steroid signal.

react_result.final_narrative_text: RaMP multi-database ORA identifies SMPDB:SMP00356 '17-Beta Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase III Deficiency' as the top pathway (rank 1, FDR 1.34e-13, 5 input hits). The same five steroid compounds hit the sibling pathways SMPDB:SMP00068 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (FDR 1.34e-13) and KEGG:map00150 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (FDR 1.34e-13). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently recovers KEGG:hsa00140 as the top hit (p=8.39e-06, 5 input hits). Mummichog m/z-network activity confirms the same cluster with MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism (p=8.40e-05, 7 steroid compounds from the 8-compound input) and adds MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as a secondary hit (p=7.56e-04, 7 compounds). The cross-paradigm consensus is therefore a coordinated perturbation of the C18/C19/C21 steroid hormone interconversion network. Tetrahydrobiopterin (C00272) appears as a single-compound hit in MUMM:biopterin_metabolism (p=0.0639, rank 5). S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (C00021) and spermidine (C00315) co-occur in MUMM:urea_cycle_amino_group_metabolism (p=0.0304, rank 2). Six driver compounds (testosterone, 17β-estradiol, estrone, dehydroepiandrosterone, 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine) map to the steroid cluster; tetrahydrobiopterin and spermidine represent secondary cofactor/polyamine signals with lower rank.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converged on a dominant steroid hormone signal. The RaMP multi-database ORA identified the Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism pathway (KEGG:map00150, SMPDB:SMP00068, FDR 1.34e-13) as the top hit, with five input steroids — testosterone (C00535), 17β-estradiol (C00951), estrone (C00468), 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one (C03917, dihydrotestosterone), and dehydroepiandrosterone (C01227) — all present in the pathway member set. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirmed the same steroid cluster through KEGG:hsa00140 (p = 8.39e-06, rank 1), with the identical five steroid hits. Mummichog m/z-network activity ranked MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism first (p = 8.40e-05), with seven of thirteen pathway-member m/z features matching the input set. MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism (p = 1.68e-04, rank 2) provided additional network corroboration. A secondary nitrogen-metabolism signal emerged from Mummichog: MUMM:urea_cycle_amino_group_metabolism (p = 0.031, rank 3) captured the S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (C00021) and spermidine (C00315) pair, while MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism (p = 0.031, rank 4) and MUMM:biopterin_metabolism (p = 0.060, rank 6) captured the tetrahydrobiopterin (C00272) and S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine pair. The biological story is a coordinated perturbation of the C18/C19/C21 steroid interconversion network as the primary treatment effect, with secondary cofactor (biopterin) and polyamine (spermidine) deregulation.
